## AnnotationError
<!-- agent: yes -->

```python
class AnnotationError(extension: str | None, error: str)
```

`tau_agent_core.entry_annotations.AnnotationError` · since 0.15.0

An ``annotate`` handler failed, or the entry's blocks could not be derived.

A handler fails by raising or by returning a value that is not JSON.
Raised after the entry is written with ``ext[<extension>] = {"error": …}``,
and the turn ends on it (docs/ENTRY-ANNOTATIONS.md §4.3).

**Constructor parameters**

- `extension: str | None` — The failing extension's name, the ``ext`` key; ``None`` when :func:`entry_blocks` raised, which every annotating extension records.
- `error: str` — ``"<ExceptionType>: <message>"``, as recorded on the entry.

`tau_agent_core.extension_auth.AuthorizationStore`

The user's authorization records, read from and written to one JSON file.

Packages are keyed by identifier and match on distribution, version and
digest. Drop-ins are keyed by resolved path and carry no version (§5).
Disables are keyed by identifier, so one covers a package and a drop-in
alike (#58).

**Constructor parameters**

- `path: Path` — The store file.
- `data: dict[str, Any]` — *(no description)*
- `existed: bool` — Whether the file was there when this store was loaded. A missing file is the first 0.14.0 start, when drop-ins are grandfathered (§5).

## BranchResult
<!-- agent: yes -->

```python
class BranchResult(ok: bool, cursor_id: str, label: str, leaf: str | None, messages: list[dict[str, Any]], error: str | None, end_reason: str | None = None, aborted_by: Literal['suspension', 'shutdown', 'signal', 'parent'] | None = None, answered_by: dict[str, Any] | None = None)
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.BranchResult`

What a sub-agent came back with (``ctx.spawn_branch``, ``AgentSession.spawn``).

A sub-agent that failed returns ``ok=False`` rather than raising: failure
containment is the design (§9.2/5), so one bad evaluator in a fan-out does not
kill the turn that spawned it. An unchecked ``ok`` turns a failure into an
empty-but-successful-looking answer.

**Constructor parameters**

- `ok: bool` — Whether the sub-agent's turn was admitted and finished, neither raising nor aborted. Read this first.
- `cursor_id: str` — The cursor its events carried; closed by the time this returns.
- `label: str` — The cursor's label: the ``label`` given, else the prompt's first 60 characters.
- `leaf: str | None` — The sub-agent's final entry id, or ``None`` if it appended nothing; the handle to read the verdict back or ``ctx.summarize_branch`` it.
- `messages: list[dict[str, Any]]` — The sub-agent turn's messages: empty when it failed or was refused, and what it wrote before the abort when it was aborted.
- `error: str | None` — Why it failed, or ``None`` when ``ok``.
- `end_reason: str | None = None` — How its turn's ``agent_end`` closed (``"done"``, ``"aborted"``, …), or ``None`` when no turn ran.
- `aborted_by: Literal['suspension', 'shutdown', 'signal', 'parent'] | None = None` — On ``end_reason == "aborted"``: ``"suspension"`` when a person answered ``abort`` at one of its suspensions, ``"shutdown"`` when the session shut down (or an RPC host's input ended) under one, ``"parent"`` when the cursor that owns it was aborted, else ``"signal"``. An aborted sub-agent is ``ok=False`` with ``error`` naming who aborted it; one stopped at a suspension was stopped by a person, so a delegating extension never retries or escalates it (docs/STEP-DEBUGGER.md §3.12.5).
- `answered_by: dict[str, Any] | None = None` — With ``aborted_by == "suspension"``, the resolution's ``answered_by``.

## ExtensionAPI
<!-- agent: yes -->

```python
class ExtensionAPI(registry: ExtensionRegistry | None = None, event_bus: EventBus | None = None, context: ExtensionContext | None = None, session: Any = None, hook_handlers: ExtensionHandlers | None = None, config: dict[str, Any] | None = None)
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionAPI`

Public API exposed to extension modules.

Reference: SUBPHASE-0.0.md, "8. Extension API Surface" section.

This is the ONLY API extension modules use. Extensions must not
import τ-agent-core internals.

**Constructor parameters**

- `registry: ExtensionRegistry | None = None` — Where tools, commands and shortcuts land; ``None`` makes a private, empty one.
- `event_bus: EventBus | None = None` — The notify bus :meth:`on` and :meth:`emit` use; ``None`` makes a private one.
- `context: ExtensionContext | None = None` — The shared context; ``None`` makes a fresh one. Either way ``session`` is bound onto it.
- `session: Any = None` — The ``AgentSession``, or ``None`` for an unbound api whose session-backed methods raise.
- `hook_handlers: ExtensionHandlers | None = None` — This extension's own runner bucket. ``None`` gives the api no identity: hook registration, :meth:`emit`, :meth:`submit` and command registration then raise.
- `config: dict[str, Any] | None = None` — This extension's config slice (:attr:`config`); deep-copied, so a handler mutating a nested value never reaches the session's config, and ``None`` reads as ``{}``.

### append_entry

```python
async append_entry(custom_type: str, data: dict) -> None
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionAPI.append_entry`

Persist durable, NON-message extension state onto the session tree (E6 §2 / S39).

Appends a ``customEntry`` node via ``AgentSession._append_custom_entry``; it
survives a reload and reads back through ``ctx.entries()``. It is NOT a
message: never folded into the loop context, never seen by the model. To
inject a node the model reads, use ``send_message`` (``visible_to_model``)
or ``send_user_message``.

**Parameters**

- `custom_type: str` — The entry's ``customType``, naming its kind; non-empty.
- `data: dict` — The state to persist.

**Raises**

- `RuntimeError` — no session with ``_append_custom_entry`` is bound (e.g. a bare ``ExtensionAPI()``); the entry is not dropped silently.
- `ValueError` — propagated from ``_append_custom_entry`` when ``custom_type`` is empty or ``data`` is not a dict.

### emit

```python
async emit(topic: str, payload: Any) -> None
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionAPI.emit`

Publish ``payload`` on this extension's channel ``ext:<name>:<topic>`` (S52).

In-RAM broadcast on the notify :class:`~tau_agent_core.events.EventBus` to
every ``api.on("ext:<name>:<topic>", handler)``; ``<name>`` is always this
extension's own. Never written to the tree, so never model-visible and
gone on restart — durable state uses :meth:`append_entry` or
:meth:`send_message`. Handlers run while this is awaited; one that raises
is surfaced through the bus's on_error path (S44), not here, unless it
runs under a policy whose outcome is ``Failed``.

**Parameters**

- `topic: str` — The topic, the last segment of the channel name.
- `payload: Any` — Delivered to each subscribed handler as-is.

**Raises**

- `ValueError` — ``topic`` is empty or whitespace.
- `RuntimeError` — No runner bucket is bound, so there is no name to namespace under.
- `HandlerPolicyError` — a policed subscriber's outcome was ``Failed``.

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionAPI.extension_name: str`

This extension's identifier (docs/EXTENSION-PACKAGES.md §2).

a package's module name, a file's stem verbatim, an inline factory's
``module.qualname``.

**Raises**

- `RuntimeError` — This api is not bound to a runner bucket, so it has no identity to qualify a name with, the same refusal :meth:`on` makes.

### on

```python
on(event: str, handler: Callable, *, policy: str | None = None) -> Callable[[], None]
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionAPI.on`

Subscribe to an event, routed by kind (S24).

See docs/extensions.md, "Hook and event vocabulary".

The mutating hooks (``ExtensionRunner.HOOK_EVENTS``: ``tool_call``,
``tool_result``, ``before_agent_start``, ``input``, ``turn_end``,
``user_turn_end``, ``session_before_switch``, ``annotate``,
``entry_written``, ``turn_setting_changed``) and the lifecycle hooks (``LIFECYCLE_EVENTS``:
``session_start``, ``session_shutdown``) go to this extension's runner
bucket, where handler errors are surfaced. Everything else — notify
events, ``"all"``, and ``ext:<name>:<topic>`` channels from :meth:`emit` —
goes to the notify ``EventBus``. Either way the handler runs as this
extension, so a ``ctx.set_model`` in it is attributed to it.

``turn_end`` fires once per agent-loop turn (per completion);
``user_turn_end`` fires once per utterance, after the loop, the followUp
drain and auto-compaction. Either handler may return ``{message}`` for a
durable append. The notify-grade ``turn_end`` ``AgentEvent`` still reaches
``api.on("all", …)``.

``policy`` names a handler policy (:meth:`register_policy`; built-ins
``gating``, ``advisory``, ``human``), which decides how the handler runs
and what its failure becomes (docs/STEP-DEBUGGER.md §4, experimental).
It is accepted on a runner-routed hook and on an ``ext:`` channel. With
no policy the handler runs exactly as it always has.

**Parameters**

- `event: str` — Event type (e.g., 'agent_start', 'tool_call', 'all').
- `handler: Callable` — Callable that receives the event (an ``AgentEvent`` for notify events; a ``(event_dict, ctx)`` pair for hook events).
- `policy: str | None = None` — A registered policy name, or ``None``.

**Returns**

An unsubscribe function.

**Raises**

- `RuntimeError` — the retired ``context`` hook (E5 §3.2 / S30), or a runner-routed hook, or a policed handler, on an api with no runner bucket (``hook_handlers is None``).
- `ValueError` — a second ``annotate`` handler from this extension, an unknown ``policy``, or a ``policy`` on a notify event.

### register_command

```python
register_command(name: str, command: dict) -> str | None
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionAPI.register_command`

Register a slash command, and try to claim ``name`` for it.

Two registrations, because there are two names (docs/EXTENSION-NAMESPACE.md).
The command is installed in the private registry at
``ext:<extension>:<name>``, where nothing can displace it, and then ``name``
itself is claimed. Claiming is first-wins: if another extension already holds
it, or a human pinned it elsewhere, this one keeps only its qualified name.

**Parameters**

- `name: str` — The command word a reader types after the ``/``.
- `command: dict` — ``{"description": str, "handler": callable, "args": str?}``.

**Returns**

``None`` when ``/name`` now runs this command. Otherwise the qualified name that holds it instead — pass it to :meth:`run_command` to wrap, chain or defer to whatever got there first.

**Raises**

- `RuntimeError` — No runner bucket is bound (:attr:`extension_name`).

### register_flow

```python
register_flow(name: str, description: str, handler: Any, *, argument: Argument | None = None, domain: Domain | None = None, values: Any = None) -> str | None
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionAPI.register_flow`

Register a slash command AND say what it takes (docs/EXTENSION-FLOWS.md).

The declaration gives the command completion, a rendered form and a
palette entry in every head. The handler is still called with
``(args, ctx)``, ``args`` being the argument's bound value as text. At
most one argument; a gesture needing several fields drives ``ui.form``.

**Parameters**

- `name: str` — The slash command. A name τ already declares is refused, because ``resolve_command`` gives a collision to the built-in and the flow would be unreachable.
- `description: str` — One line, shown in completion, the palette and ``/help``.
- `handler: Any` — The callable ``(args, ctx)``, sync or async, as :meth:`register_command` takes.
- `argument: Argument | None = None` — What the command takes, or ``None`` for one that takes nothing.
- `domain: Domain | None = None` — The argument's domain, when it is not one τ already declares. Its ``name`` must be what ``argument.domain`` says.
- `values: Any = None` — How ``domain``'s values are found, when it names an enumerator: a callable ``(query, limit) -> [(value, label)]``. Not needed for a domain that is ``free`` or has fixed ``values``.

**Returns**

meth:`register_command` returns — ``None`` when ``/name`` is this flow, else the qualified name that holds it. The flow itself is always reachable at ``ext:<extension>:<name>``.

**Raises**

- `ValueError` — ``name`` or ``description`` is empty; ``handler`` is not callable; ``name`` is already a built-in flow or view; ``domain`` does not match what ``argument`` names; a domain with an enumerator has no ``values`` callable; or an ``argument`` came with ``values`` but no ``domain``.
- `RuntimeError` — No runner bucket is bound (:attr:`extension_name`).

### register_policy

```python
register_policy(name: str, policy: HandlerPolicy) -> None
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionAPI.register_policy`

Register a handler policy for ``api.on(..., policy=name)``, session-wide (§4).

Experimental: below 1.0 names and defaults may change. ``gating``,
``advisory`` and ``human`` are built in. A policy is removed with the
extension that registered it (disable or reload); a handler that already
named it keeps it.

**Parameters**

- `name: str` — The name handlers register under.
- `policy: HandlerPolicy` — Anything with ``async run(call, site) -> Outcome``; see :class:`~tau_agent_core.policies.HandlerPolicy`.

**Raises**

- `ValueError` — a blank name, or one already registered.
- `TypeError` — ``policy`` has no callable ``run``.

### register_shortcut

```python
register_shortcut(key: str, command: str, *, args: str = '', description: str | None = None) -> None
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionAPI.register_shortcut`

Bind a key to a command in the guarded extension chord namespace (E10 §6 / S69).

``key`` is the chord tail after the ``ctrl+e`` extension leader, so an
extension cannot clobber a core binding: ``key="g"`` with
``command="fleet_status"`` makes ``ctrl+e g`` dispatch ``/fleet_status``,
exactly as a panel action or a typed command would.

**Parameters**

- `key: str` — The chord-tail key (e.g. ``"g"``, ``"1"``). A non-empty token with no whitespace.
- `command: str` — The name of the command to dispatch (a ``register_command`` name). Not required to exist yet at registration time — an unknown command surfaces at dispatch (``handled=False``), like a panel action.
- `args: str = ''` — Argument string passed to the command's handler (default ``""``), the same slot a typed ``/name args`` fills.
- `description: str | None = None` — Optional label for the chord menu / palette entry; falls back to the command's own registered description when omitted.

**Raises**

- `ValueError` — ``key`` or ``command`` is not a non-empty string, or ``key`` contains whitespace (a chord tail is a single key token — Fail-Early rather than silently binding an unreachable key).
- `TypeError` — ``args`` is not a string, or ``description`` is neither a string nor ``None``.

### register_tool

```python
register_tool(definition: dict | ExtensionToolDefinition) -> None
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionAPI.register_tool`

Register a tool callable by the LLM.

The definition is validated into an
:class:`~tau_agent_core.tools.base.ExtensionToolDefinition` with
``source="extension"`` and stored in the registry; the tool joins the
loop's tools next turn.

**Parameters**

- `definition: dict | ExtensionToolDefinition` — A dict or an ``ExtensionToolDefinition``. Required keys: ``name``; ``description`` (sent to the LLM); ``parameters`` (a JSON-schema dict); ``execute(tool_call_id, params, signal, on_update, ctx)``, sync or async, returning an ``AgentToolResult``-shaped value, with ``ctx`` the bound ``ExtensionContext``. Optional: ``label`` (defaults to ``name``), ``prompt_snippet``, ``prompt_guidelines``, ``execution_mode`` (``"sequential"``/``"parallel"``). A dict is not mutated.

**Raises**

- `ValueError` — if a required key is missing.
- `TypeError` — if ``parameters`` is not a dict or ``execute`` is not callable.

### request

```python
async request(topic: str, payload: Any, *, timeout_s: float) -> list[RequestReply]
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionAPI.request`

Ask every subscriber of ``ext:<name>:<topic>`` and collect each answer (docs/EXT-REQUEST.md).

The requester's terms replace each subscriber's own policy for this
call: every subscriber runs under a ``timeout_s`` deadline, and a timeout
or an error is :class:`~tau_agent_core.policies.Failed`. A subscriber
registered under ``advisory`` cannot turn that into ``Proceeded``.

Subscribers run concurrently, each deadline starting at once, so the
whole call takes at most ``timeout_s`` of their own time. A suspension
inside a subscriber pauses its clock (docs/STEP-DEBUGGER.md §4.3), and an
enclosing deadline caps all of them. A sync subscriber runs on a worker
thread and is abandoned at the deadline (#97). ``payload`` is passed
as-is to each, as by :meth:`emit`.

**Parameters**

- `topic: str` — The topic, the last segment of the channel name.
- `payload: Any` — Delivered to each subscriber.
- `timeout_s: float` — Each subscriber's budget in seconds; positive and finite.

**Returns**

class:`~tau_agent_core.policies.RequestReply` per subscriber, in subscription order; ``[]`` with none, which the caller judges.

**Raises**

- `ValueError` — an empty ``topic`` or a bad ``timeout_s``.
- `RuntimeError` — no runner bucket is bound, so there is no channel name.
- `TurnSuspended` — a subscriber suspended; the others are cancelled.

### request_user_action

```python
async request_user_action(sentence: str, *, lock: bool = False, ask: dict[str, Any] | None = None, release: str | None = None) -> str
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionAPI.request_user_action`

Stop the session, put a request in front of whoever is attached, or both.

Reference: docs/EXTENSION-LOCKS.md. Appends the one reserved
``customEntry`` (:data:`~tau_agent_core.extension_locks.REQUEST_ENTRY_TYPE`)
carrying this extension's identity. Two independent keys, so four states
(§3): ``lock`` refuses the next submission at this cursor; ``ask`` is a
spec every head can render. Neither blocks a coroutine and neither
survives on anything but the tree, which is why both survive a restart
and why a user can branch around either.

**Parameters**

- `sentence: str` — The one line a head shows under τ's own framing label.
- `lock: bool = False` — Refuse submissions while the cursor is this entry.
- `ask: dict[str, Any] | None = None` — A spec for :func:`validate_ask_spec` — body, optional fields, and the actions naming the commands that answer it.
- `release: str | None = None` — The command name that clears the lock, shown as the way out. Advisory: commands are exempt from a lock by WHERE the check sits (§5), not by matching this name.

**Returns**

The appended entry's id — the request id an action is dispatched with, and what :meth:`~tau_agent_core.agent_session.AgentSession.answer_request` takes.

**Raises**

- `RuntimeError` — this api is bound to no runner bucket, so it has no extension identity to append under (Fail-Early: the identity is stored in the entry, and the case this exists for is a reload where nobody can be asked for it).
- `ValueError` — from :func:`validate_ask_spec` on a malformed ask, or from :func:`~tau_agent_core.extension_locks.build_request_data` on an entry that neither locks nor asks.

```python
resumed() -> dict[str, Any] | None
```

```python
async run_command(name: str, args: str = '') -> Any
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionAPI.run_command`

Run a registered command by either of its names and return its output.

The composition seam. An extension that was refused a typed name, or that
wants to extend another's behaviour, calls the qualified name — resolved HERE,
at call time, so a disabled extension is a name that no longer answers rather
than a captured callable that still runs.

**Parameters**

- `name: str` — A typed or qualified command name.
- `args: str = ''` — The argument string, exactly as a reader would have typed it.

Whatever the command's handler returned.

### send_message

```python
async send_message(message: dict, options: dict | None = None) -> None
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionAPI.send_message`

Append a durable custom message node onto the active path (E6 §2 / S38).

Persisted as a ``role: "custom"`` tree node via
``AgentSession._append_custom_message``; it renders in the transcript and
survives a reload, like a ``before_agent_start`` injection.

**Parameters**

- `message: dict` — ``{customType, content, display?, details?}``.
- `options: dict | None = None` — ``{"visible_to_model": True}`` also feeds the node to the model (as a user message on the wire). By default (D-E6-1) it is display-only and never reaches the LLM; ``before_agent_start`` and ``send_user_message`` are the model-visible channels.

**Raises**

- `RuntimeError` — no session with ``_append_custom_message`` is bound (e.g. a bare ``ExtensionAPI()``); the message is not dropped silently.
- `ValueError` — propagated from ``_append_custom_message`` when ``message`` lacks ``content`` or ``customType``.

### send_user_message

```python
send_user_message(content: str, deliver_as: str = 'followUp') -> None
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionAPI.send_user_message`

Queue a user message for the agent.

**Parameters**

- `content: str` — The message text.
- `deliver_as: str = 'followUp'` — The delivery mode; a plain ``str`` so modes stay extensible (decision 5), validated against the three the queue supports. ``"followUp"`` drains at the end of the current ``prompt()`` and re-enters within the same call. ``"nextTurn"`` waits for the next ``prompt()``. ``"steer"`` (docs/SUBMISSION-LIFECYCLE.md phase 4) is delivered by the loop running now, before its next LLM call — how a hook steers the turn it runs inside, which a submission cannot.

**Raises**

- `ValueError` — if ``deliver_as`` is not ``"followUp"``, ``"nextTurn"`` or ``"steer"``.
- `RuntimeError` — if no session with a message queue is bound (e.g. a bare ``ExtensionAPI()`` with no session). Fail-Early: raise rather than silently drop the message (the old ``hasattr`` no-op).

Name the session (:func:`apply_session_name`, shared with the RPC verb).

### set_warning

```python
set_warning(key: str, message: str, severity: str = 'warning') -> None
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionAPI.set_warning`

Set this extension's warning ``key`` on the session until cleared (#60).

It stays readable by every head and by a client attaching later, and is
shown once through ``ui.notify`` when new or changed, and again after a
session swap. Setting the same key replaces it. It persists across
new, fork and switch until cleared; a disable or a reload clears it.

Safe from a worker thread: the warning is checked on the calling thread.
While the session's loop runs, the write goes onto that loop, returns
before it lands, and a listener's exception reaches the loop's handler,
not the caller; otherwise it applies at once on the calling thread. It
never moves the session onto the caller's loop.

**Parameters**

- `key: str` — The warning's name within this extension.
- `message: str` — One line.
- `severity: str = 'warning'` — ``"warning"`` or ``"error"``.

**Raises**

- `RuntimeError` — this api is not bound to a session or to a loaded extension.
- `ValueError` — the extension is named ``tau``, which τ reserves; a non-string or blank key or message; a message of more than one line; or an unknown severity.

### submit

```python
async submit(text: str, *, multitask_strategy: MultitaskStrategy = 'reject', images: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None, correlation: dict[str, Any] | None = None, allow_user_input: bool = False, cursor: Any = None) -> SubmissionResult
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionAPI.submit`

Originate an agent turn as THIS extension (docs/SUBMISSION-LIFECYCLE.md).

Goes through :meth:`AgentSession.submit`, the one admission point. Not
parameters, so not forgeable: ``source="extension"``, ``submitter`` (this
extension's own name), ``expand_commands=False`` (a ``/compact`` in a bus
payload stays text) and ``depth`` (derived; a self-continuing chain raises
past ``MAX_SUBMISSION_DEPTH``). Call from the session's own loop; a
thread or foreign loop uses :meth:`submit_threadsafe`.

**Parameters**

- `text: str` — The utterance to run a turn on.
- `multitask_strategy: MultitaskStrategy = 'reject'` — Policy against an in-flight turn, as :meth:`AgentSession.submit` defines them. ``"reject"`` by default: a busy session returns ``accepted=False``, never a silent queue.
- `images: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None` — Optional image dicts for a multimodal submission.
- `correlation: dict[str, Any] | None = None` — JSON-safe origin detail (bus subject, cron id, request id) carried onto every event this turn emits.
- `allow_user_input: bool = False` — Whether code under this submission may prompt a human (Jupyter's ``allow_stdin``). ``False`` by default: for the whole turn :meth:`ExtensionUI.form` skips the TUI delegate and takes the headless policy, raising :class:`HeadlessDialogError` without one.
- `cursor: Any = None` — The live cursor the turn extends (``ctx.cursors``), so a strategy acts on that cursor's lock and queues. ``None`` is the head's cursor, which is not the cursor of the turn that called this unless the head ran it.

**Returns**

class:`~tau_agent_core.submission.SubmissionResult`: ``accepted`` plus this turn's ``messages`` or a ``rejection_reason``. A refusal is a result, not an exception.

**Raises**

- `RuntimeError` — No runner bucket (no identity) or no ``AgentSession`` is bound; or :meth:`AgentSession.submit` refused the call (off its loop, reentrant on the in-flight turn's task, or past ``MAX_SUBMISSION_DEPTH``).
- `NotImplementedError` — An unknown ``multitask_strategy``.
- `ValueError` — ``correlation`` carries a non-JSON value.

### submit_threadsafe

```python
submit_threadsafe(text: str, *, multitask_strategy: MultitaskStrategy = 'reject', images: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None, correlation: dict[str, Any] | None = None, allow_user_input: bool = False) -> concurrent.futures.Future[SubmissionResult]
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionAPI.submit_threadsafe`

Originate a turn from a FOREIGN loop or thread (docs/SUBMISSION-LIFECYCLE.md).

Synchronous: hands the submission to the session's own loop
(:meth:`AgentSession.submit_threadsafe`) and returns a future. Use it when
the callback runs on a thread the library spawned (``paho-mqtt``,
``watchdog``, a WSGI thread, ``threading.Timer``); a callback awaited on
the session's loop (``nats-py`` connected from ``session_start``) uses
:meth:`submit`. The fixed fields are :meth:`submit`'s.

**Parameters**

- `text: str` — The utterance to run a turn on.
- `multitask_strategy: MultitaskStrategy = 'reject'` — Policy against an in-flight turn; ``"reject"`` by default, as for :meth:`submit`.
- `images: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None` — Optional image dicts for a multimodal submission.
- `correlation: dict[str, Any] | None = None` — JSON-safe origin detail carried onto every event of the turn, as for :meth:`submit`.
- `allow_user_input: bool = False` — Whether code under this submission may prompt a human; ``False`` by default, as for :meth:`submit`.

**Returns**

class:`concurrent.futures.Future` resolving to the class:`~tau_agent_core.submission.SubmissionResult`. Block on it with ``.result(timeout=…)`` if the driver thread wants the answer; drop it for fire-and-forget (a failure is still surfaced through the session's extension-error sink, never swallowed).

**Raises**

- `RuntimeError` — No runner bucket or no ``AgentSession`` is bound; the session is not bound to a running loop yet; or this is called from the session's own loop, where blocking on the future deadlocks.
- `ValueError` — ``correlation`` carries a non-JSON value.

### suspend

```python
async suspend(spec: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionAPI.suspend` · since 0.15.0

Stop the running turn until a responder answers ``spec`` (docs/STEP-DEBUGGER.md §3).

Permitted only where everything the turn produced is already in the
tree: a top-level ``tool_call``, ``entry_written``, ``turn_end`` and
``user_turn_end``, and an ``ext:`` handler reached from one of them
(:meth:`can_suspend_here`). A durable ``suspension`` side entry is
written under the cursor's leaf, ``suspension_open`` reaches every head,
and every enclosing policy deadline pauses until this returns, time
queued behind another suspension on the cursor included. Picking
``abort`` also aborts the turn; the turn's abort resolves it, and every
suspension queued behind it, as ``abort``.

**Parameters**

- `spec: dict[str, Any]` — :func:`validate_ask_spec`'s spec (``title``, a body, ``fields``, ``actions``) plus ``evidence``, a list of ``{label, text}``, and ``targetId``, the entry it is about.

**Returns**

``{id, action, values, answered_by, at_ms}``. ``id`` is ``None`` when the turn was already aborted, and nothing was raised.

**Raises**

- `ValueError` — a malformed spec.
- `SuspensionRefused` — not a suspension site, or a turn that cannot be stepped (``store_history`` off, a read-only session).
- `NoResponderError` — nothing can answer it (§3.8).

### suspend_refusal

```python
suspend_refusal() -> str | None
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionAPI.suspend_refusal` · since 0.15.0

Why a suspension raised in this turn could not be answered, or ``None`` (§3.8, §3.9).

The reason :meth:`can_suspend` reads false for, worded for a person: no
turn running, ``store_history`` off, a read-only session, no live
responder, or a submission (a child's root's) without
``allow_user_input``. An armed ``input`` hook returns it as its
``{"refuse": …}``.

**Returns**

The reason, or ``None`` when a suspension could be raised.

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionAPI.ui: ExtensionUI`

The session's one :class:`ExtensionUI`, the same object as ``ctx.ui``.

Painted in the TUI; headless it emits records or stderr lines, and

```python
unregister_command(name: str) -> None
```

Withdraw one of THIS extension's commands, and any typed name bound to it.

## ExtensionCapabilityError
<!-- agent: yes -->

`tau_agent_core.sdk.ExtensionCapabilityError`

A bus-touching extension's declaration is missing or cannot be honoured.

Raised at the factory, before ``register(api)`` runs (H8: "refuse rather
than discover"). Two distinct causes share this type because both are the
same failure — a declaration nobody validated — one at the writing end
and one at the checking end:

- the module sets ``TOUCHES_BUS = True`` but ``SUBJECTS`` is absent, empty,
  or not a sequence of non-empty strings (H7: "a silent omission is a load
  error rather than a hole in the diff");
- the module declares ``TOUCHES_BUS = True`` and valid ``SUBJECTS``, but the
  session it is loading into has no bus transport
  (``bus_available=False``) — a declared capability the session cannot
  back, refused rather than loaded and left to fail silently the first
  time a handler reaches for a bus it does not have.
- the module declares ``CONFIG_SCHEMA`` and it is not a valid form spec.
  Same discipline: a schema nobody can render is a load error, not a
  settings screen that comes up empty.

```python
class ExtensionContext(cwd: str = '.', signal: Any | None = None)
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionContext`

Context passed to extension event handlers and tools.

Reference: SUBPHASE-0.0.md, "8. Extension API Surface" section.

**Constructor parameters**

- `cwd: str = '.'` — Returned by :attr:`cwd` as given; nothing resolves it. The default ``"."`` is the process cwd, for a context made outside a session.
- `signal: Any | None = None` — The abort signal :attr:`signal` returns while no session is bound.

### abort

```python
abort() -> None
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionContext.abort`

Trip :attr:`signal`, the running turn's, as an ``"extension"`` abort.

The loop stops at its next check; followUps queued for this turn still
run, each on a fresh signal (docs/TURN-SETTINGS.md §5). No-op without a signal.

### compact

```python
async compact(custom_instructions: str | None = None, defer: bool = False) -> Any
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionContext.compact`

Compact the active conversation (delegates to ``AgentSession.compact``).

Summarizes the active path's prefix via the LLM and APPENDS a compaction
entry, so the prefix drops out of future context at read time.

**Parameters**

- `custom_instructions: str | None = None` — Optional extra focus for the summary.
- `defer: bool = False` — Record the intent instead of compacting now (S20 / decision 3). A tool calling this mid-turn cannot compact under the live agent loop; the intent is applied exactly once at the tail of ``prompt()``, the same site as auto-compaction.

**Returns**

The ``CompactionResult``, or ``None`` when there was nothing to compact or ``defer`` was set.

**Raises**

- `RuntimeError` — No session is bound.
- `CompactionError` — Summary generation failed (not when deferred).

### complete

```python
async complete(messages: list[dict[str, Any]], *, model: Any = None, constraints: Any = None, api_key: str | None = None) -> Any
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionContext.complete`

One LLM request/response — no agent loop, no tree writes (C1).

Touches neither the entry log nor the cursor, so it is safe under
``asyncio.gather`` at any fan-out; its usage is banked on the session's
side ledger. No retries. With ``constraints``::

    verdicts = await asyncio.gather(*[
        ctx.complete(
            [{"role": "user", "content": f"Include {doc}?"}],
            model="local-llm-small",
            constraints=DecodeConstraints(choices=["include", "exclude"]),
        )
        for doc in docs
    ])

Each verdict is constraint-verified by the provider, so a server that dropped the
grammar raises rather than returning free prose as a verdict.

**Parameters**

- `messages: list[dict[str, Any]]` — τ message dicts (``{"role": ..., "content": ...}``).
- `model: Any = None` — model name (resolved via the config registry), a ``Model``, or None for the session's current model.
- `constraints: Any = None` — an optional ``tau_llm.DecodeConstraints``.
- `api_key: str | None = None` — overrides the key ``AgentSession.model_and_key`` gives ``model``.

**Returns**

A ``tau_llm.AssistantMessage``.

**Raises**

- `RuntimeError` — No session is bound; ``model`` is a name and the session has no resolver; the completion errored or was aborted; or it stopped at the token limit (``stop_reason="length"``), which is a truncated prefix rather than an answer.
- `ConstraintViolation` — the constraint did not hold (see DecodeConstraints).

### complete_text

```python
async complete_text(messages: list[dict[str, Any]], *, model: Any = None, constraints: Any = None, api_key: str | None = None) -> str
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionContext.complete_text`

Run :meth:`complete` and return the response's text (the common case).

**Parameters**

- `messages: list[dict[str, Any]]` — τ message dicts, as for :meth:`complete`.
- `model: Any = None` — A name, a ``Model``, or ``None`` for the session's, as for :meth:`complete`.
- `constraints: Any = None` — An optional ``tau_llm.DecodeConstraints``.
- `api_key: str | None = None` — Overrides the model's key, as for :meth:`complete`.

**Returns**

The text blocks joined, VERBATIM: under a constraint whitespace is part of the constrained value (``grammar.fixed("yes ")`` forces the trailing space), so stripping would yield a string the constraint never produced.

**Raises**

- `RuntimeError` — the response's text is empty or whitespace-only, or :meth:`complete` failed.
- `ConstraintViolation` — the constraint did not hold.

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionContext.cursor: Any`

The :class:`~tau_agent_core.cursor.Cursor` this handler acts on.

Inside a turn, that turn's cursor; outside one, the head's. ``ctx.cursor.leaf``

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionContext.cursors: tuple[Any, ...]`

Every live cursor on the bound session, the head's included, oldest first.

A cursor absent from here was closed: a finished sub-agent, a client's
cursor under ``tau serve``, or a head cursor a swap retired.

### fork

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionContext.fork`

Fork the conversation in place or into a new session file.

**Parameters**

- `entry_id: str | None = None` — Where to fork. In place, the entry to move onto (``None`` is before the root); for export, the entry whose path is copied (``None`` copies the whole session).
- `mode: Literal['in_place', 'export'] = 'in_place'` — ``"in_place"`` moves the session's head cursor so the next turn appends a sibling branch there. ``"export"`` copies the session into a NEW file via ``Session.fork``, never touching the source.
- `defer: bool = False` — Record the intent instead of forking now; it is applied once at the tail of ``prompt()``. A tool calling this mid-turn needs it.

**Returns**

In place, the context at the new position; for export, the new session file's path as a string; ``None`` when ``defer`` is set.

**Raises**

- `RuntimeError` — no session is bound, or export from a log that is not file-backed.
- `ValueError` — an unknown ``mode``, or an ``entry_id`` that names no entry.

### spawn_branch

```python
async spawn_branch(parent_id: str | None, prompt: str | None = None, *, seed: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None, tools: list[str], model: Any = None, max_turns: int | None = None, label: str | None = None, system_prompt: str | None = None, hooks: bool = True) -> 'BranchResult'
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionContext.spawn_branch`

Run a tool-using sub-agent on its own cursor in THIS conversation (C2/W14).

Delegates to :meth:`AgentSession.spawn` (docs/CURSORS.md §6). From inside a
tool, seed the branch instead of prompting it, and hang it from the parent
of the calling message, whose call is still unanswered
(docs/SEEDED-BRANCHES.md)::

    parent = next(e["parentId"] for e in ctx.entries() if e["id"] == ctx.cursor.leaf)
    note = {"customType": "planner", "content": "You are the sub-agent now."}
    result = await ctx.spawn_branch(
        parent, seed=[note, *seed_tool_call("start_subagent", {}, task)],
        tools=["write"], model="mistral-small",
    )

**Parameters**

- `parent_id: str | None` — The entry the sub-agent's cursor opens at, or ``None`` for before the root.
- `prompt: str | None = None` — The sub-agent's task as a user message; ``None`` needs ``seed``.
- `seed: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None` — Messages written on the branch before the prompt; with no prompt the sub-agent answers them (``tau_agent_core.seed``).
- `tools: list[str]` — A required hard allowlist of tool names; ``[]`` means none.
- `model: Any = None` — A config name, a ``Model``, or ``None`` for the session's; the key goes with it (``AgentSession.model_and_key``).
- `max_turns: int | None = None` — Cap on the sub-agent's loop turns, or ``None`` for no cap.
- `label: str | None = None` — The cursor's label; defaults to the prompt's first 60 characters.
- `system_prompt: str | None = None` — Replaces the session's system prompt for this branch.
- `hooks: bool = True` — Whether extension hooks fire in the sub-agent's turn; ``False`` mutes them.

**Returns**

class:`BranchResult`. **Check ``ok``** — a failed sub-agent returns a result, it does not raise.

**Raises**

- `RuntimeError` — No session is bound, or ``model`` is a name and the session has no resolver.
- `ValueError` — a tool is not one the spawning turn offers; ``parent_id`` names no entry; neither ``prompt`` nor ``seed`` is given; or the seed is malformed or leaves a tool call unanswered (named by id).

### summarize_branch

```python
async summarize_branch(from_entry: str, custom_instructions: str | None = None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionContext.summarize_branch`

Summarize the subtree at ``from_entry`` and splice it onto the active path.

Binds :func:`tau_agent_core.tree_ops.summarize_and_navigate` to the session's
head cursor, model and key, and banks the tokens the summarizer spent. It
APPENDs a ``branch_summary`` entry parented at ``from_entry``; the abandoned
children drop out of context via the ``parentId`` walk.

**Parameters**

- `from_entry: str` — The entry whose subtree is summarized.
- `custom_instructions: str | None = None` — Optional extra focus for the summary.

**Returns**

The re-rendered active-path messages (``ConversationTree.context_for``).

**Raises**

- `RuntimeError` — No session is bound.
- `ValueError` — ``from_entry`` names no entry (checked before the model call), or the summarizer returned nothing usable.
- `ModelUnavailableError` — the session's model is unavailable.

## ExtensionUI
<!-- agent: yes -->

```python
class ExtensionUI(headless_policy: dict[str, str] | None = None)
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionUI`

User interaction surfaces: notify, status, panel, form.

Reference: SUBPHASE-0.0.md, "8. Extension API Surface"; docs/EXTENSION-LOCKS.md §8.

Every surface here DESCRIBES itself on the headless record stream and, where
it can act, acts through a named command. ``confirm``/``select``/``input``
were the exception — they emitted nothing and answered only through a bound
TUI delegate — and are gone: an extension that wants an answer declares an
ASK (``api.request_user_action``), which every head renders and which does
not hold the turn lock while a human thinks.

:meth:`form` is the one blocking dialog left, and it is not the way to ask a
human a question that gates work; it is the way a FLOW collects a missing
argument from whoever typed the command. Headless it obeys the
:meth:`set_headless_defaults` policy — ``form=defaults`` returns each field's
declared default, no policy RAISES :class:`HeadlessDialogError` — because
silently auto-filling a form nobody filled would fabricate consent.

**A bound delegate is not enough on its own** (docs/SUBMISSION-LIFECYCLE.md,
``Submission.allow_user_input`` — Jupyter's ``allow_stdin``). A form reaches
the delegate only if the submission driving the calling code permits it:
:func:`~tau_agent_core.submission.user_input_permitted` is ``False`` for the
whole of a turn admitted with ``allow_user_input=False``, and the form then
takes the headless-answer route even though a delegate and a live human
exist. That is what makes the capability per-SUBMISSION rather than
per-process: one embedded τ can serve an interactive session and a
cron-triggered submission at the same time, and only the latter is barred
from opening a dialog.

``notify``, ``set_status`` and ``panel`` are non-blocking (no answer to
fabricate), so they are NOT gated by ``allow_user_input``, which is about
asking a human rather than telling one.

**Constructor parameters**

- `headless_policy: dict[str, str] | None = None` — Optional ``{method: token}`` headless-answer map (validated via :meth:`set_headless_defaults`). Defaults to no policy → a headless form raises (S48).

<path|null>, "constraints": <summary>}``. Like :meth:`emit_veto` it never

**Parameters**

- `source: str | None = None` — The calling extension's path, or ``None`` if unattributed.

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionUI.emit_veto`

Emit a blocked-tool VETO record on the headless JSON stream (E7 §3 / S50).

Routes ONLY to the record sink — the ``--mode json`` record family (S49) —
emitting ``{"type": "extension", "kind": "veto", "extension": <path|null>,
"tool": <name>, "reason": <reason>, "blocked": true}`` so a parent
orchestrating a child ``tau -p --mode json`` can tell a `tool_call` veto
(anchor G11) from a generic errored tool result. Deliberately does NOT touch
the TUI delegate or stderr: in the TUI the veto is rendered off the
``tool_execution_end`` AgentEvent's ``blocked`` field, and in ``--mode text``
it already surfaces as the persisted errored tool-result node — a stderr line
here would be a duplicate. With no sink installed this is a no-op.

**Parameters**

- `extension: str | None` — The vetoing extension's path, or ``None`` if unattributed.
- `tool: str` — The blocked tool's name.
- `reason: str` — The veto reason the hook gave.

### form

```python
async form(spec: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any] | None
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionUI.form`

Show a declarative form and return ``{field_name: value}`` (E10 §6 / S66).

The spec is validated before any UI is shown, in every mode. Routing:

- a bound delegate and a driving submission that permits asking a human
  (:meth:`_human_delegate`) → the TUI's ``ExtensionFormScreen``;
- otherwise, with a record sink installed (``--mode json``), one
  ``{"type": "extension", "kind": "form", …}`` record is emitted first;
- then the headless policy: ``form=defaults`` answers each field with
  :func:`form_headless_value`, and no policy raises.

**Parameters**

- `spec: dict[str, Any]` — The form spec :func:`validate_form_spec` accepts; ``kind`` is one of :data:`FORM_FIELD_KINDS`.

**Returns**

Each field name mapped to its answer, or ``None`` when a TUI user cancels (never a fabricated set of answers). The headless ``defaults`` answer is always a dict.

**Raises**

- `ValueError` — ``spec`` is malformed.
- `HeadlessDialogError` — no human may be asked and there is no ``form`` policy.

### interactive

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionUI.interactive: bool`

Whether a human is watching a live surface right now.

``True`` only in TUI mode with a bound delegate — the one case that can
paint something (``set_status``/``panel``/``notify``) without producing a
stderr line or a JSON record instead. Extension code with a
high-frequency ambient update (an ASR partial, a tick) checks this
BEFORE formatting or calling ``set_status``/``panel``, so a headless
run — including ``--mode json``, whose record schema has no room for
arbitrary per-partial noise — pays nothing for updates nobody can see.

Unlike :meth:`_human_delegate` this does not consult
``user_input_permitted()``: that gate is permission to ask a human a
blocking question mid-submission, not whether a screen exists to paint
ambient state on.

### notify

```python

```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.ExtensionUI.notify`

Show a notification.

Routing (first match wins):

- **TUI mode** with a delegate → paints on the delegate (the Textual toast).
- **headless ``--mode json``** (a :meth:`set_record_sink` is installed) →
  emits one ``{"type": "extension", "kind": "notify", …}`` record through the
  sink instead of stderr, so extension activity is visible in the JSON event
  stream (S49 — anchor G10).
- otherwise (headless ``--mode text`` / SDK) → prints to stderr, unchanged.

**Parameters**

- `message: str` — The notification text.
- `level: str = 'info'` — Severity label passed to the delegate or written into the record or stderr line, e.g. ``"info"``.
- `source: str | None = None` — The originating extension's identity when the caller knows it (the S44 error-surface path passes the failing extension's path). A plain ``api.ui.notify(...)`` cannot supply one, because every extension shares the session's one :class:`ExtensionUI`; the record then carries ``"extension": null`` rather than a fabricated name.

Pressing an action dispatches its ``command`` as a registered command. The
spec is validated before any UI is shown, in every mode. Non-blocking, so
it routes like :meth:`notify`: the delegate's panel host in the TUI; one
``{"type": "extension", "kind": "panel", "key": …, "spec": …}`` record
under ``--mode json`` (``spec`` normalized, or ``null`` on clear), whose
actions cannot be pressed; otherwise the title on stderr.

**Parameters**

- `key: str` — The panel; re-calling the same key updates it in place.
- `spec: dict[str, Any] | None` — ``{title?, <body>, actions?}`` as :func:`validate_panel_spec` accepts; ``None`` clears the panel.
- `source: str | None = None` — The originating extension's identity, or ``None``; same contract as :meth:`notify`'s.

## HeadlessDialogError
<!-- agent: yes -->

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.HeadlessDialogError`

A UI dialog was opened with no human reachable and no explicit ``--ui-defaults`` policy.

Raised by :meth:`ExtensionUI.form` — the one blocking dialog left after
docs/EXTENSION-LOCKS.md §8.2 — when it has no headless-answer policy (E7 §3 /
S48) and no human can be asked. "No human can be asked" has TWO causes, and
this one exception covers both because the consequence is identical:

- **headless mode** — there is no TUI delegate at all;
- **``allow_user_input=False``** — a delegate may well exist, but the
  submission driving this code declared that code running under it may not
  prompt a human (Jupyter's ``allow_stdin``;
  docs/SUBMISSION-LIFECYCLE.md "The dataclasses", which names this class as
  the enforcement: *"Enforcement stays HeadlessDialogError"*). A cron- or
  bus-originated turn in a TUI process is exactly this case.

Either way, silently auto-answering would fabricate consent for whatever the
dialog was gating — so Fail-Early: raise, naming the opt-in that restores an
explicit auto-answer.

## PausableDeadline
<!-- agent: yes -->

```python
class PausableDeadline(seconds: float)
```

`tau_agent_core.policies.PausableDeadline` · since 0.15.0

A time budget for one call, run in its own task and cancelled when the budget is spent.

:meth:`run` starts the clock; :meth:`pause` and :meth:`resume` stop and
restart it, and nest. A deadline resumed with no time left fires at once.
An enclosing deadline caps this one: when it expires, its cancellation
reaches this deadline's task, and the enclosing policy's timeout applies.

**Constructor parameters**

- `seconds: float` — The budget; positive and finite.

### expired

`tau_agent_core.policies.PausableDeadline.expired` · since 0.15.0

Whether it fired and cancelled its call.

### pause

```python
pause() -> None
```

`tau_agent_core.policies.PausableDeadline.pause` · since 0.15.0

Stop the clock; nested pauses need as many :meth:`resume` calls.

### paused

`tau_agent_core.policies.PausableDeadline.paused: bool` · since 0.15.0

Whether at least one :meth:`pause` is outstanding.

### remaining

```python
remaining() -> float
```

`tau_agent_core.policies.PausableDeadline.remaining` · since 0.15.0

Seconds left before this call is cancelled, capped by every enclosing deadline.

**Returns**

The smallest time left among this deadline and its enclosing ones; zero or less once spent.

### resume

```python
resume() -> None
```

`tau_agent_core.policies.PausableDeadline.resume` · since 0.15.0

Undo one :meth:`pause`; the last one restarts the clock, firing at once if none is left.

**Raises**

- `RuntimeError` — there is no outstanding pause.

### run

```python
async run(call: Callable[[], Awaitable[Any]]) -> Any
```

`tau_agent_core.policies.PausableDeadline.run` · since 0.15.0

Run ``call`` in its own task under this deadline and return its value.

The task copies the current context, with this deadline appended to
the :func:`enclosing_deadlines` of the code that calls this. Any exception, ``BaseException`` included,
leaves unchanged; only this deadline's own cancellation becomes
:class:`DeadlineExpired`.

**Parameters**

- `call: Callable[[], Awaitable[Any]]` — Called once, in the new task.

**Returns**

What ``call`` returned.

**Raises**

- `DeadlineExpired` — the deadline fired first.
- `RuntimeError` — this deadline already ran a call.

## plan_extensions
<!-- agent: yes -->

```python

```

`tau_agent_core.sdk.plan_extensions`

Decide which extensions load, from metadata and paths alone (docs/EXTENSION-PACKAGES.md §5).

Discovered drop-ins load first, then discovered packages, then the ``-e``
values in argument order. A discovered source loads only with an
authorization record and no disable (#58); a disabled one is withheld as
``disabled`` before anything else is checked. An ``-e`` value is authorized
by being named, overrides a disable, and claims its identifier first: a discovered source with the same identifier
but another target is withheld as a ``collision``, as is a later
discovered source whose identifier an earlier one already claimed. Two
routes to one file load once.

**Parameters**

- `explicit: Sequence[str] = ()` — The ``-e`` values (paths or module names).
- `discover: bool = True` — Whether to discover at all; ``--no-extensions`` sets False.
- `extensions_dir: str | Path | None = None` — The drop-in directory; ``None`` is :func:`~tau_agent_core.extension_sources.default_extensions_dir`.
- `store_path: str | Path | None = None` — The authorization store; ``None`` is the file beside ``extensions_dir``.
- `write: bool = True` — Whether a missing store may be created to grandfather the drop-ins present. A listing passes False.

**Returns**

The plan.

**Raises**

- `ValueError` — An ``-e`` value resolves to nothing, or is ambiguous.
- `AuthorizationStoreError` — The store exists and cannot be read.

## runs_on_behalf_of
<!-- agent: yes -->

```python

```

`tau_agent_core.policies.runs_on_behalf_of` · since 0.15.0

Whether the current task is ``task``, or a policed task that ``task`` is awaiting.

A bounded handler runs in its own task, so a guard that compares
``asyncio.current_task()`` with a turn's task would miss it. This follows
each :meth:`PausableDeadline.run` task to the task awaiting it. A task a
handler merely spawned is not followed, so it is never mistaken for the
turn. A sync handler's worker thread (#97) has no task; it counts as its
deadline's task until that deadline abandons it.

**Parameters**

- `task: asyncio.Task[Any]` — The task to test against, e.g. the one driving a turn.

**Returns**

True when the current code runs as part of ``task``.

- `spec: Any` — ``{title?: str, fields: [field, ...]}``; each field is ``{name: str, kind: str, label?: str, default?: Any, options?: [str, ...]}``. A ``select``/``multiselect`` field must carry non-empty string ``options``.

**Returns**

The title (default ``"Form"``) and the normalized fields: ``label`` defaulted to ``name``, ``default``/``options`` kept when present.

**Raises**

- `ValueError` — a non-dict spec, a non-string title or label, an empty or absent ``fields`` list, a field without a non-empty string ``name``, a duplicate name, an unknown ``kind``, or a select/multiselect without valid ``options``. Nothing is silently dropped.

## validate_form_values
<!-- agent: yes -->

```python
validate_form_values(fields: list[dict[str, Any]], values: dict[str, Any]) -> None
```

`tau_agent_core.extension_types.validate_form_values`

Check answered values against the fields :func:`validate_form_spec` returned.

The reverse direction of the form contract: ``validate_form_spec`` says what
may be asked, this says whether an answer is admissible. Used where a form's
answers become durable state — an extension's config slice — rather than a
one-shot return value.

**Parameters**

- `fields: list[dict[str, Any]]` — The normalized field list, as returned by :func:`validate_form_spec`.
- `values: dict[str, Any]` — The answers, keyed by field name. Every declared field must be present; missing is not the same as empty and is not filled in here.

**Raises**

- `ValueError` — an undeclared key, a missing declared field, a value whose type does not match its kind, or a ``select``/``multiselect`` value outside its declared options. Fail-Early: nothing is coerced and nothing is dropped.


`tau_agent_core.extension_types.validate_panel_spec`

Validate + normalize a ``ui.panel`` spec into ``{title, body, actions}`` (S68).

Shared by :meth:`ExtensionUI.panel` and the TUI's ``ExtensionPanel`` widget.

**Parameters**

- `spec: Any` — ``{title?: str, <body>, actions?: [...]}`` where ``<body>`` is EXACTLY ONE of ``table`` / ``list`` / ``text`` (see :func:`_validate_panel_body`) and ``actions`` is the optional command-dispatch list (see :func:`_validate_panel_actions`).

**Returns**

``{"title", "body", "actions"}``; title defaults to ``"Panel"``, actions to ``[]``.

**Raises**

- `ValueError` — a non-dict spec, a non-string title, zero or several body keys, or any malformed body or action.

## validate_suspension_spec
<!-- agent: yes -->

```python
validate_suspension_spec(spec: Any) -> dict[str, Any]
```

`tau_agent_core.suspensions.validate_suspension_spec` · since 0.15.0

Validate and normalize an ``api.suspend`` spec: the ask spec's shape, plus ``evidence`` and ``targetId``.

``title``, the optional body (``text``, ``list`` or ``table``) and
``fields`` are the ask spec's (:func:`~tau_agent_core.extension_types.validate_ask_spec`).
An action is ``{label}`` alone: a suspension's answer is returned to the
code that raised it, so no action names a command, unlike an ask's.

**Parameters**

- `spec: Any` — ``{title?, text|list|table?, fields?, actions, evidence?, targetId?}``. ``evidence`` is a list of ``{label, text}`` strings; ``targetId`` the id of the entry the suspension is about.

**Returns**

``{title, body, fields, actions, evidence, targetId}``; ``body`` and ``targetId`` are ``None`` and ``evidence`` ``[]`` when absent.

**Raises**

- `ValueError` — a malformed body or field (as for an ask), no actions, an action that is not exactly ``{label}``, a repeated label, or a malformed ``evidence`` or ``targetId``.
